item.title: Parking, 17th October
item.description:
Cars parked on corners. Cars double parked. Cars parked inconsiderately. Council are quick enough to send letters to residents for the following reason; Dear Sir/Madam Highways Act 1980 Section 149 Obstruction to Public Highway 020892 \ 5373 area where this had occurred. Anything unlawfully deposited on the highway constitutes a danger or nuisance, including obstructing the view of users of the highway will be removed without notice by the Royal Greenwich and any costs involved will be sort by Royal Greenwich council for reimbursement. Please refrain from placing traffic cones, wheelie bins or any other material in the carriageway to secure parking. I am relying on your co-operation and avoid the necessity for any further action. Thanking you in advance for your co-operation with regards to this matter. Yours sincerely, Highway Inspector For context; Bins were put across the roadway to prevent parking as the council were cutting trees and shrubbery by the fencing, and would’ve been prevented doing so by parked cars. The council were also supposed to come back to collect rubbish, but never did. Some homeowners have installed parking posts on their private parking bay, but they have been tampered with. It has become much worse since the post office and bus garage restricted the amount of parking spaces for employees. The “social housing residents” in new flats opposite are (according to the building management) using Goldfinch Road for parking. I think that’s an outrageous claim for them to make - why do they believe only “social housing residents” are parking in Goldfinch Road? This is an ongoing, daily issue.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Goldfinch Road, Thamesmead
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Street bin collection - issue not resolved, 17th October
item.description:
I reported the council’s street bin collection being stored in a location where there is a clear fly-tipping warning sign. The rubbish is attracting crows and potentially other pests and wildlife, leaving food waste scattered around the area. My FixMyStreet report has been marked as “fixed”, presumably because the council may have arranged more frequent collections. However, this does not address the food waste and rubbish already left behind, nor does it resolve the problem caused by storing the bins in this location. The issue has not been resolved simply by collecting the bins more frequently. The area needs to be cleaned thoroughly, and a more suitable location for the street bins must be found to prevent this from happening again. Please arrange for the remaining food waste and rubbish to be cleared, review the suitability of the current bin storage location, and stop using this spot if it continues to attract vermin and other pests. Please do not mark this issue as resolved until the underlying problem has actually been addressed.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 1, Burham Close, Penge, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
